newsitem.title: USA: SEC says reaches agreement muni banker Mark Ferber.
newsitem.headline: SEC says reaches agreement muni banker Mark Ferber.

text.p: The SEC said Thursday that it reached an agreement with municipal banker Mark Ferber, a former partner with Lazard Freres & Co, that bars him from the industry and requires him to pay a $650,000 fine.
The SEC announced the agreement while it filed a complaint against Ferber in Federal court here.

Ferber was convicted in August on 58 out of 61 counts of fraud and corruption charges and is awaiting sentencing. On Wednesday a federal judge during a sentence hearing dropped 11 of the 58 counts and said he is mulling a 33-month sentence.

The SEC complaint alleges that Feber on behalf of Lazard Freres negotiated a "lucrative contract with Merrill Lynch (Co), which provided that Lazard and Merrill Lynch would jointly market interest rate swaps and that Lazard would be a consultant to Merrill Lynch."
The SEC complaint said that "pursuant to the contract between September 1990 and 1992, Merrill Lynch paid Lazard nearly $5.8 million which resulted in a substantial financial benefit to Ferber."

The SEC complaint futher alleges that the contract with Merrill Lynch was a "material fact that should have been dislosed to Lazard's finacial advisory clients that were serviced by Ferber and were considering the selection of Merrill Lynch as a provider of financial services."
The SEC listed the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority, the District of Columbia and the U.S Postal Service as clients.
Ferber was convicted in August on fraud and corruption charges involving a retainer and swap fee-splitting arrangement with Merrill Lynch.
The allegations centered on whether or not a contract between Ferber and Merrill Lynch was adequately disclosed to Ferber's government clients in the municipal bond market.

Merrill Lynch and Lazard Freres settled with the U.S. Attorneys Office late last year over the matter, paying a total of $24 million in fines. Neither firm admitted or denied guilt in connection with the settlement.

Federal Judge William Young is expected to finish Ferber's sentencing hearing on Thursday. Ferber, who was not in the courtroom on Wednesday, has agreed not to appeal the sentence or file any post-trial motions in exchange for a lower sentence. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
